documents.title: CU Committee Report: Generative Artificial Intelligence for Education and Pedagogy
documents.summary: The 2023 committee report from Cornell's provost-convened group sets out why instructors should rethink learning outcomes for generative AI and recommends that each instructor choose among prohibiting, allowing with attribution, or encouraging use. It adds disciplinary examples (including programming), privacy and IP cautions, a recommendation against relying on detectors, and recommendations to faculty and administrators.
documents.stance_why: The report proposes 'a flexible framework in which instructors can choose to prohibit, to allow with attribution, or to encourage GAI use', and recommends that the Code give 'individual faculty ... authority to determine when its use is prohibited, attributed, or encouraged'. It sets no single rule, so the stance is delegates with three named options.
